title: Coroner's inquest into First Nation women's death in Kenora, Ont., slated to start today
summary: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a 29-year-old Alberta woman at Lake of the Woods District Hospital (LWDH) in Kenora, Ont., is expected to start later Monday morning. Here is what we know about…

image.caption: Lake of the Woods District Hospital in Kenora, Ont., is seen in this July 2026 photo. Kaylee Martha Dallas Crowchild died at the hospital on Sept. 20, 2022 following an incident at the Kenora District Jail. (Sarah Law/CBC)

blocks.text: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a 29-year-old Alberta woman at Lake of the Woods District Hospital (LWDH) in Kenora, Ont., is expected to start later Monday morning. Here is what we know about the upcoming proceedings.
Kaylee Martha Dallas Crowchild of Tsuut’ina Nation died on Sept. 20, 2022
A coroner’s inquest into the death of a 29-year-old Alberta woman at Lake of the Woods District Hospital (LWDH) in Kenora, Ont., is expected to start later Monday morning.

Kaylee Martha Dallas Crowchild was a member of Tsuut’ina Nation, a Dene community in southern Alberta. She died at the hospital on Sept. 20, 2022 following an incident at the Kenora District Jail, according to a news release issued by Ontario’s Ministry of the Solicitor General last month.
More than four years later, an inquest into her death is being held via video conference. Inquests are mandatory under the provincial Coroners Act when a person dies in custody.
CBC News has reached out to Crowchild’s family for comment on the upcoming proceedings and is awaiting a response.

blocks.text: In a coroner’s inquest, witnesses provide information about the circumstances surrounding a person’s death, after which a five-person jury is tasked with identifying who died, when and where the person died, their medical cause of death and means of death.
Jurors will then classify how the death happened: due to natural causes, accident, homicide, suicide or undetermined.
While jurors cannot make any legal findings or lay blame on anyone, they may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.

blocks.text: The proceedings come about five months after a coroner's inquest into the death of Percy Adam Henry, a 27-year-old who died at LWDH on Feb. 8, 2021 after being transferred from the Kenora District Jail. He grew up in Naotkamegwanning First Nation, formerly known as Whitefish Bay, and was a member of Wabaseemoong Independent Nations.
Crowchild’s inquest is set to start at 10 a.m. ET and last six days.
Jurors are expected to hear from about 11 witnesses. Dr. John Carlisle will be the presiding officer, while Robert Kozak, Jenna Simpson and Makenzie Chan will serve as inquest counsel.
People can watch a livestream of the proceedings online here.

Sarah Law is a CBC News reporter based in Thunder Bay, Ont., and has also worked for newspapers and online publications elsewhere in the province. Have a story tip? You can reach her at sarah.law@cbc.ca.
